coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED (in order of authority):
(1) 2011 BCS National Championship Bowl Media Guide, published by Alabama Athletics ~Jan 6, 2012 — i.e. the staff as it stood AT the Jan 9, 2012 title game. This is the single best source for the ring rule. URL: https://s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/sidearm.nextgen.sites/rolltide.com/documents/2012/1/6/2011-bcs-bowl-guide.pdf?timestamp=20160610115907 . Its "Support Staff" photo grid (printed p. 58) contains 33 named support staffers; the "Coaching Staff" bio section (pp. 36-57) covers Saban + 9 on-field assistants + Cochran, Marynowitz, Pannunzio, Allen, Springer, Sherrer, Martin.
(2) 2011 Alabama Football Media Guide (preseason), archive.org: https://archive.org/download/alabama-football-2011-media-guide-4/Alabama%20Football%202011%20Media%20Guide%204.pdf — same structure, "Football Support" grid on printed p. 102 (32 people).
(3) rolltide.com coaching list archived on the Wayback Machine Dec 20, 2011 (three weeks before the title game): http://web.archive.org/web/20111220221933/http://www.rolltide.com:80/sports/m-footbl/mtt/alab-m-footbl-mtt.html — 13 coaches, clean selectable HTML text.
(4) Wikipedia team-season page and individual Wikipedia bios.

TOTAL: 52 people documented.

QUOTE LIMITATIONS — PLEASE READ:
- The support-staff pages in BOTH official guides render every name and job title as a RASTER NAMEPLATE GRAPHIC baked into the photo. There is no selectable text layer for those 33 people. Per instructions, quote is set to "" for those source entries and the exact nameplate wording is transcribed in the note field instead. I read every nameplate by rendering the PDF pages at 200-800 DPI and inspecting them visually; the two guides agree on every title, which cross-validates the readings.
- Where a source DOES have selectable text (the archived rolltide.com HTML page, the media guide bio pages, Wikipedia), I supplied real verbatim quotes.
- Media-guide PDF quotes are single lines from the embedded text layer, chosen to avoid line-break splits. The bowl guide's own text layer mangles ligatures ("Off ensive", "Jeff  Stoutland", "fi rst"), so I did not quote from it.
- Russ Callaway's Wikipedia quote contains the typo "ifor" — reproduced verbatim as required.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT:
- Glenn Schumann and Rob Ezell appear on the Wikipedia team-season page (graduate assistant / student assistant) but appear in NEITHER official guide's staff grid. Their Wikipedia bios independently confirm 2011 Alabama service. Lower confidence on exact 2011 title than the other 50; flagged in their notes.
- No archived rolltide.com support-staff/analyst directory page was recoverable — the Wayback CDX API returned 503 repeatedly, and the one archived football page (the roster page) lists only the 13 primary coaches. So the support-staff evidence rests entirely on the two PDF guides.
- Undergraduate student managers, additional student assistants, video interns, and any GA hired after the guides went to press are almost certainly missing. The real headcount was larger than 52.
- I deliberately EXCLUDED athletics-department-wide administrators listed in the guides' "2011 Alabama Football Directory" because they are not football-program staff: Mal Moore (Athletics Director), Finus Gaston, Shane Lyons, Milton Overton, Kevin Almond, Chris Besanceney, Jon Dever, Dr. Kevin Whitacker, Carol Park, Jeff Purinton (Assoc. AD/Football Communications), Marie Robbins, Ronny Robertson, Doug Walker, Mike Ward, Jon Gilbert, Dave Hart. Purinton and Walker are football-facing communications staff if the dataset wants them; flagging so the decision is yours, not mine.
- Terry Saban is described in the guide's Saban feature but holds no staff title; excluded.

ROSTER-CHANGE NOTES: Candice Rosenkranz appears in the January 2012 bowl guide but NOT the preseason media guide, so she joined during the season and was present at the title game. Jim McElwain was named Colorado State head coach on Dec 12, 2011 but coached the championship game. Sal Sunseri left for Tennessee on Jan 13, 2012 — four days AFTER the title game, so he was on staff for it. No documented mid-season departures.
